title: Low-Cost Early Detection of Crop Water Stress via Remote Sensing
background: Smallholder farms in semi-arid regions lose significant yield to water stress that is detected too late. Satellite data is free but coarse; ground sensors are accurate but expensive to deploy at scale. There is a need for an affordable, scalable system that detects crop water stress days before visible symptoms appear, so farmers can act in time.
objectives: Detect crop water stress at least 3-5 days before visible wilting.
Achieve field-level accuracy usable for irrigation decisions on smallholder plots (< 2 hectares).
Keep per-farm hardware and operating cost affordable for smallholders.
Provide actionable, interpretable alerts to non-expert users.
constraints: Intermittent internet connectivity in target regions.
No access to expensive hyperspectral satellites or manned aircraft.
Solution must scale to thousands of farms without per-farm calibration by an expert.
expected_outputs: A clear system architecture (sensing + data + model + alerting).
A validation plan with quantified accuracy/lead-time targets.
evaluation_notes: An excellent answer fuses free multispectral satellite data (e.g. Sentinel-2) with a small number of cheap ground/edge sensors, uses a physically-grounded or well-validated ML model, quantifies lead time and accuracy, addresses connectivity/power constraints explicitly, and gives a credible cost and scaling plan. Reward genuine novelty in sensor fusion, self-calibration, or interpretability. Penalize hand-waving, ignored constraints, and unvalidated accuracy claims.
